attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post; the cited figures are his own arithmetic and conclusion.

semantics.note: Keeps 'I don't think' and the financing reasoning. Coming right after 'pretty obvious when you do the maths', this is a firm belief about the present, not graded probability, so it is a scorable observation.

contract.note: Reading 'not many' as a small share of the cohort's capacity in physical construction is ordinary and fair. Using Q4 2025 as the baseline is reasonable. Because 'not many' has no threshold, the interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Wood Mackenzie source for 241 GW and 33% active development. It gives no construction-only breakdown, so it cannot test the claim.
Sightline covers a different population (projects since 2024 due in 2026) and a later date. It is not matched to the 61 GW cohort.
JLL's 35 GW North American construction pipeline is contrary context. It uses a different geography and coverage and has no crosswalk to the cohort.

reviews.rationale: No item gives a construction-status breakdown of the Wood Mackenzie active-development cohort. Sightline and JLL measure different populations and point in opposite directions. The packet cannot show whether only a small share of the roughly 61 GW was under physical construction.

attribution.note: Zitron's own argument in his own post.

semantics.note: Captures the causal claim that build time is understated and is a cause beyond power. It leaves out the supporting 3GW figure, which is fine because that figure is supporting evidence, not the claim itself.

contract.note: Requiring material overruns beyond power, plus understated public representations, matches 'way longer than anybody is letting on'. Rightly declines to read 'anybody' literally.

evidence.note: Global JLL data on 2025 construction delays and equipment lead times. It suggests non-power constraints but does not show that representations understated US build durations.
Crusoe's own disclosure of its target to energize the first Abilene phase in H1 2025. This is a schedule baseline only.
Crusoe says the first two buildings were energized within a year, on target. This counts against his example, but it is one company's self-report on one phase.
A Sightline analyst reports 2025 slippage and an industry that is cagey about timelines. It does not isolate construction time from power and other causes.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows widespread delays and long equipment lead times, but no matched project records that separate construction time from power and other causes, or that show public schedules understated build times. The Abilene example ran on schedule by the company's own account. Taken together, the evidence does not settle the causal claim.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: Preserves 'often', 'rarely aligns', 'guaranteeing' and the skim-or-delegate outcome. It is a broad causal chain about reviewing LLM code.

contract.note: Requiring evidence of each link (verbosity and standards failures, longer review, then skimming or delegation) fits the stated chain. Defining 'far longer' per comparable change is a fair reading.

evidence.note: Meta trial of AI patches for review comments, run in 2024. The review slowdown disappeared after a UX change. That challenges inevitability in a narrow setting but does not represent generated code in general.
Sonar survey: 38% say AI code takes more review effort, 27% say less. Self-reported effort does not measure review time, standards compliance or skimming.

reviews.rationale: No representative measure of verbosity, compliance with in-house standards, matched review time or reviewer skimming or delegation exists in the packet. The Meta trial is narrow and dated, and the survey is self-reported and mixed. Neither establishes or refutes the causal chain.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Mostly faithful. 'These things' refers to the debt-funded deals discussed in the passage, and 'AI data centers' slightly broadens that. The either/or structure and the interest consequence are kept.

contract.note: Comparing against original schedules and requiring delay-linked extra interest is a fair reading of 'piling up'. However, the cohort, baseline and interest measure are all evaluator choices.

evidence.note: Sightline reports 11 GW with no visible construction and 26% slippage in 2025. These are aggregate figures from before the window, not matched to the debt-funded projects, with no interest data.
Nebius's own disclosure of interest-bearing notes. It shows no overdue milestone and no interest attributable to delay.

reviews.rationale: The packet has aggregate signs of delay and one disclosure of interest-bearing debt. It has no project-level link between schedule slippage, outstanding debt and extra interest in March 2026, so the causal and financial claim is not settled.
